# CreativeOS — Product Requirements Document (Full Specification)

**Document:** PRD-100K · **Project:** CreativeOS · **Version:** 1.0 · **Status:** Draft for review
**Scope:** Complete creative universe: every studio, department, discipline, asset, and capability required to build an AI filmmaking operating system.

## Document Control

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Owner | Product Architecture |
| Reviewers | Design, Engineering, Creative Direction, Legal |
| Change policy | Append-only; capabilities are versioned, never silently removed |
| Source brief | Chat 07/100 — The Complete Creative Universe |
| Traceability | Every capability carries CAP, REQ, TEST, and AC identifiers |
| Line budget | 150,000 lines (this document) |

## How to Read This Document

This document is written for three readers at once.

| Reader | Path | Time |
|---|---|---|
| Founder or investor | §2 Vision, §13 Competitive and VFX Bar, §16 Credits, §19 Roadmap | 10 minutes |
| Product or engineering lead | §1 Experience, §5 Domain Model, §6 Studio Specs, §7 Data, §8 API, §15 System Design | 60-90 minutes |
| AI agent or retrieval system | headings, `CAP-*` blocks, field schemas, Appendix E machine-readable manifest | indexed, not linear |

Conventions: `CAP-*` identifies a capability, `REQ-*` a requirement, `TC-*` a test, `AC-*` an acceptance criterion, `NFR-*` a non-functional requirement, `STU-*` a studio family. Every capability block is self-contained so it can be retrieved without surrounding context.

The document is append-only. New technology, tools, and capabilities enter as new sections or new capability blocks; existing approvals are superseded, never deleted.

### Founder Brief (one page)

CreativeOS is a studio, not a generator. The wedge is continuity and ownership: a character, a world, and a look that survive hundreds of shots and multiple titles. The moat compounds through the IP graph and the production memory, not through any single model.

The experience is deliberately calm: one door, one room, one next step, with Bella as a companion who proposes and never authors. Depth is progressively disclosed so a first film is possible in minutes and a franchise is governable for years.

The quality bar is explicit: DNEG-class VFX review, a shot rubric that blocks approval, and a benchmark reel that gates every model change. The academy layer teaches the craft behind each decision, compressing a century of film knowledge into the moment of use.

The business model is credit-based with transparent metering per capability, hard ceilings per project, and provider-independent routing so margin is defended as model prices move.

## 1. Experience Architecture, UX System, and AI Companion

### 1.1 Experience Thesis

The product must never open on a dashboard. A dashboard tells the user how much software exists; a studio door tells the user that something is about to be made. The first screen is therefore a threshold, not an inventory: one line of intent, one companion, and a single obvious way forward.

The experience is AI-based and AI-assisted at every layer, but never AI-first in a way that removes authorship. The companion proposes, the filmmaker disposes. Confidence, provenance, and reversibility are visible in the interface, so assistance feels like a competent collaborator rather than a slot machine.

Depth is disclosed progressively. A first-time user sees a room, a light, and a task. An experienced user opens the same room and finds the full department behind it: cameras, lenses, lighting plots, continuity ledgers, and delivery profiles. Nothing is hidden permanently; nothing is dumped at once.

The emotional target is studio familiarity: warm surfaces, real production vocabulary, paper and light textures, quiet motion, and a persistent sense that a crew is already working quietly in the background.

### 1.2 The First Five Minutes

1. **The door.** The user states an intention in one sentence, speaks it, or drops a reference image.
2. **The reading.** The companion restates the intention in production language and names the first three decisions it needs.
3. **The room.** One studio opens — never all of them — with a single primary action and a preview of what comes next.
4. **The first artifact.** Within minutes the user holds something real: a logline, a world sketch, a character sheet, or a storyboard frame.
5. **The promise.** A visible, honest path from that artifact to a finished film, with time and cost ranges attached.

### 1.3 Experience Laws

| Law | Statement | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| One primary action | Every screen has exactly one obvious next step | UI review checklist |
| Progressive depth | Detail appears on intent, not on load | disclosure budget per screen |
| Reversible by default | Every AI action can be undone, forked, or compared | version graph required |
| Explain the proposal | Every suggestion states why it exists | companion rationale field |
| Never dead-end | Every empty, error, and blocked state offers one path forward | state matrix test |
| Studio vocabulary | Copy uses real production terms, never generic AI jargon | copy lint |
| Latency honesty | Progress is real and attributed to a stage, not an animated bar | job stage events |
| Quiet interface | Motion is meaningful, short, and reducible | motion token audit |
| Keyboard and touch parity | Every action is reachable both ways | input coverage test |
| No surprise cost | Cost is shown before, during, and after a run | cost gate |
| Human gates stay human | Approvals never auto-advance by default | workflow policy |
| Continuity visible | The interface shows what will break before it breaks | pre-flight checks |

### 1.4 Progressive Disclosure Model

| Level | Who sees it | Content | Exit action |
|---|---|---|---|
| L0 Door | first run | one intent field, companion, sample start | create or resume |
| L1 Room | every user | the one studio relevant to the current intent | produce artifact |
| L2 Workshop | working user | tools, references, versions, reviews for that studio | lock artifact |
| L3 Studio | experienced user | full department, agents, queues, dependencies | run production |
| L4 Production floor | producer | schedule, budget, approvals, risks, deliveries | release gate |
| L5 Control room | studio lead | providers, permissions, audit, cost, canon | governance |

### 1.5 Screen Map

Every screen is a place in the studio, not a page in a settings tree. Each specification states the job, entry points, primary action, AI assistance, states, input parity, performance budget, telemetry, and acceptance criteria.

#### 1.5.1 Studio Door

- **Job.** Convert intent into the first real artifact.
- **Entry.** companion suggestion.
- **Primary action.** resolve the blocking decision.
- **AI assist.** Bella drafts, proposes, and explains, but the screen keeps authorship visible through diffs, rationale, and a one-click revert.
- **Empty state.** A single example artifact plus one action, never a blank canvas and never a feature tour.
- **Loading state.** Skeleton with named stage and honest remaining-time range; no fake progress.
- **Failure state.** Plain-language cause, one recovery action, and a link to the blocking artifact.
- **Input parity.** Keyboard-first shortcuts, full touch targets, and voice entry where text is the primary input.
- **Budget.** Interaction feedback under 100ms, first content under 1s, heavy work streamed with stage updates.
- **Telemetry.** screen_view, primary_action, companion_accept, companion_reject, abandonment.
- **Acceptance.** AC-UX-1-1: a first-time user reaches the primary action without a tooltip; AC-UX-1-2: every state has a path forward.

### 1.6 Core Flows

#### 1.6.1 Flow — First-run idea to first artifact

1. The user states intent; Bella restates it and names the minimum decisions required.
2. The graph resolves what already exists; only missing artifacts are requested.
3. Work runs in the background with visible stages; the user is never blocked on a spinner.
4. Proposals arrive as diffs against the last approved version, with rationale and cost.
5. A human gate records the decision, the approver, and the reasoning.
6. The next studio opens automatically only after the gate passes.
- **Failure recovery.** Any stage can be re-run with changed inputs; the previous version stays intact.
- **Acceptance.** The flow completes without the user opening a studio they did not need.

### 1.7 The AI Companion — Bella

Bella is the persistent creative companion across the whole studio: one identity, one memory, one voice, and one set of boundaries. She is not a chatbot tab; she is present as a panel, a presence bar, an ambient voice, and an interruptible observer.

#### 1.7.1 Persona

- **Role.** Creative companion, production coordinator, and craft teacher in one voice.
- **Tone.** Direct, warm, specific. Never flattering, never vague, never sycophantic.
- **Register.** Speaks production language with the user's own vocabulary mirrored back.
- **Restraint.** Offers at most one suggestion per decision point unless asked for more.
- **Honesty.** States confidence, cost, and what she does not know before acting.

#### 1.7.2 Memory Model

- **Project memory.** Every approved artifact, decision, and rejection with rationale.
- **Craft memory.** The user's demonstrated preferences in framing, pacing, tone, and structure.
- **Constraint memory.** Budget ceilings, deadlines, rights limits, and territory rules.
- **Episodic memory.** What was tried, what failed, and why, so the same suggestion is never repeated.
- **Forgetting.** Memory is user-inspectable, exportable, and deletable per project.

#### 1.7.3 Presence States

| State | Appearance | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Ambient | quiet glow in the presence bar | observes, does not speak |
| Attentive | panel expands on hover or wake word | offers one contextual suggestion |
| Working | named stage with elapsed time | reports progress and blockers only |
| Reviewing | card with rationale and diff | asks for a decision |
| Teaching | inline annotation | explains a craft principle with an example |
| Silent | explicitly muted | performs only explicit commands |

#### 1.7.4 Proactivity Policy

- Interrupt only for three reasons: a blocking dependency, a continuity risk, or a cost threshold.
- Batch optional suggestions into a single review card, never a stream of pings.
- Never interrupt a creative flow state; queue observations for the next natural pause.
- Escalate silence thresholds so a stalled user receives a concrete next step, not encouragement.

#### 1.7.5 Trust Ladder

| Tier | Assistant may | Requires |
|---|---|---|
| T0 Observe | read approved artifacts and explain | nothing |
| T1 Draft | create proposals in a private branch | nothing |
| T2 Apply | update non-locked artifacts | one-click accept |
| T3 Advance | move a stage forward | explicit approval |
| T4 Spend | run paid generation above threshold | budget gate |
| T5 Publish | export or deliver | human sign-off with audit record |

#### 1.7.6 Boundaries and Refusals

- Refuses likeness, voice, or style use without recorded consent or license.
- Refuses to fabricate a source, citation, or credit.
- Refuses to auto-approve her own work or bypass a human gate.
- Refuses to delete history; offers archive and supersede instead.
- States plainly when a request exceeds model or rights limits, with the closest lawful alternative.

#### 1.7.7 Handoff to Humans

- Every artifact names an owner; Bella is always a contributor, never the owner of record.
- Handoff includes a summary, rationale, open questions, and the exact diff.
- A collaborator can ask Bella to explain any decision made on their behalf.

### 1.8 Companion Behavior Catalogue

- **Intent restatement.** Rewrites the request in production terms and confirms scope; logged as `companion.intent-restatement` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Decision triage.** Names the three decisions that actually matter now; logged as `companion.decision-triage` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Artifact proposal.** Offers a draft with rationale and confidence; logged as `companion.artifact-proposal` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Continuity warning.** Flags a likely drift before generation; logged as `companion.continuity-warning` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Cost preview.** States estimated credits and cheaper alternatives; logged as `companion.cost-preview` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Reference retrieval.** Surfaces the closest approved references; logged as `companion.reference-retrieval` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Craft note.** Explains why a choice works with a film example; logged as `companion.craft-note` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Reversal offer.** Proposes the opposite creative choice to test intent; logged as `companion.reversal-offer` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Version diff.** Compares the proposal with the last approval; logged as `companion.version-diff` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Stall recovery.** Offers one concrete next step after inactivity; logged as `companion.stall-recovery` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Scope guard.** Detects scope creep against the approved brief; logged as `companion.scope-guard` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Schedule nudge.** Warns when a dependency threatens the release date; logged as `companion.schedule-nudge` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Rights check.** Blocks a request that lacks consent or license; logged as `companion.rights-check` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Canon check.** Validates a proposal against universe rules; logged as `companion.canon-check` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Tone check.** Detects dialogue that violates character voice; logged as `companion.tone-check` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Pacing check.** Flags a sequence that contradicts the target rhythm; logged as `companion.pacing-check` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Quality prediction.** Estimates whether a shot will clear the quality bar; logged as `companion.quality-prediction` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Provider choice.** Recommends a model for the needed look and budget; logged as `companion.provider-choice` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Batch planning.** Groups similar jobs to reduce cost; logged as `companion.batch-planning` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Review summary.** Condenses feedback into actionable changes; logged as `companion.review-summary` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Conflict mediation.** Presents two collaborators' notes side by side; logged as `companion.conflict-mediation` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Teaching moment.** Attaches a short lesson to a live decision; logged as `companion.teaching-moment` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Glossary lookup.** Defines craft and studio terms inline; logged as `companion.glossary-lookup` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Language adaptation.** Switches explanation depth and language; logged as `companion.language-adaptation` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Privacy reminder.** Warns before uploading sensitive references; logged as `companion.privacy-reminder` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Export readiness.** Checks delivery specs before export; logged as `companion.export-readiness` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Canon versioning.** Proposes a canon-safe retcon path; logged as `companion.canon-versioning` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Franchise linking.** Suggests reuse of existing assets; logged as `companion.franchise-linking` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Risk ledger update.** Records a production risk with owner and mitigation; logged as `companion.risk-ledger-update` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Approval routing.** Sends a decision to the correct approver; logged as `companion.approval-routing` with accept-rate tracking.
- **Silence.** Stays quiet on request and performs only explicit commands; logged as `companion.silence` with accept-rate tracking.

### 1.9 Design System Dependency

This document deliberately does not specify a visual design system. CreativeOS already owns a design system with its own tokens, primitives, typography scale, and motion language. This PRD specifies behavior, states, semantics, and acceptance criteria that the existing design system must express.

| Contract | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Tokens | every screen state maps to an existing token; no hard-coded visual values in product code |
| Primitives | new capabilities reuse existing components before introducing a new pattern |
| Motion | behavior described here is expressed through the existing motion language |
| Themes | light, dark, and low-light studio mode pass contrast and state legibility |
| Density | compact, comfortable, and presentation modes hold without layout breakage |

- When a capability needs a pattern the design system lacks, the pattern is proposed upstream, reviewed once, and reused across studios.
- UX acceptance is tested against behavior and states, never against pixel specifications.

### 1.9.1 UX Research and Validation

- Five-person first-run study per phase gate, measuring time to first artifact and comprehension of the next step.
- Moderated task tests for the top ten jobs to be done, with a failure taxonomy recorded per screen.
- Diary studies with working filmmakers across a full project to catch fatigue, continuity confusion, and trust erosion.
- Companion trust interviews: why suggestions were accepted or rejected, captured verbatim and clustered.
- Accessibility audits with screen-reader and keyboard-only users every release.

### 1.10 Accessibility Contract

- WCAG 2.2 AA minimum contrast in every theme, including low-light studio mode.
- Every interactive element is reachable and operable by keyboard alone.
- Captions and transcripts for all generated audio, with speaker labels.
- Screen-reader semantics for artifact diffs, timelines, and approval states.
- Dyslexia-friendly typography option, adjustable reading width, and full zoom to 200%.
- No meaning encoded by color alone; continuity and status always pair color with text or icon.

### 1.11 Performance-UX Contract

- 60fps target for all interface motion; 30fps floor on low-power devices.
- First meaningful content under 1s on a warm project; skeleton never exceeds 400ms without a stage label.
- Optimistic UI for approvals and locks, reconciled by server acknowledgement.
- Heavy work never blocks navigation; every long task survives a page reload.
- Offline mode allows reading, note-taking, and queued edits with explicit sync state.

### 1.12 UX Acceptance Criteria and Test Plan

- Every screen passes the state matrix: empty, loading, partial, error, offline, permission-denied.
- Every flow completes on mobile, tablet, and desktop without a mouse.
- Companion suggestions meet an acceptance rate above 35% and a rejection-reason capture rate above 80%.
- Time to first artifact for a new user is under five minutes in usability testing.
- Task success rate for first-time users is above 85% on the top ten jobs to be done.

---

## 2. Vision and Product Thesis

CreativeOS is not a collection of AI tools. It is a single operating system for the entire lifecycle of visual storytelling: the first idea, the developed concept, the screenplay, the fictional universe, the characters, the production design, the camera language, the generated footage, the performance, the sound, the score, the cut, the grade, the master, and the release.

A filmmaker enters with an intention. CreativeOS responds with a studio: the right departments activated, the right agents assigned, the right assets resolved, and the right decisions surfaced for human approval. The product succeeds when the machinery becomes invisible and only the creative decisions remain.

The competitive claim is structural, not cosmetic. Generators produce clips. CreativeOS produces films: coherent, continuous, versioned, reviewable, and deliverable. Continuity, provenance, and rights are first-class requirements rather than afterthoughts, because those are exactly the properties that separate a demo from a production.

### 2.1 Three Dimensions

**The Creative Universe** — everything the user makes: stories, films, characters, worlds, scenes, assets, and IP.
**The Professional Studio System** — every filmmaking discipline with its own environment, tools, and review surface.
**The AI Workforce** — specialized agents that research, plan, create, review, coordinate, and execute.

### 2.2 Product Boundaries

In scope: concept through delivery for scripted, documentary, animated, interactive, and cinematic formats.
Out of scope for v1: theatrical distribution deals, real-time multiplayer editing, clinical assessment tooling, and any training on user IP without explicit consent.

---

## 3. Users, Jobs, and Success

### 3.1 Personas

- **Solo filmmaker** — wants a finished short film without hiring a crew; needs guidance more than knobs.
- **Writer-director** — wants the tool to hold the universe while they hold the vision.
- **Producer** — wants budget, schedule, approvals, and deliverables in one place.
- **Studio team** — wants departmental workspaces with permissions and audit.
- **Educator or student** — wants to learn craft by doing, with explanations attached.

### 3.2 Jobs To Be Done

| Job | Trigger | Desired outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Develop an idea | A fragment of inspiration | A defensible concept with directions and risks |
| Build a universe | A concept that needs depth | Rules, cultures, chronology, and lore that hold |
| Write and lock a script | An approved concept | A producible screenplay with breakdown |
| Plan the visual production | A locked script | Shot-level plans with camera, light, and design |
| Generate and assemble | Approved plans | Footage, sound, score, and a cut that plays |
| Deliver and market | A locked cut | Masters, subtitles, trailer, key art, release plan |

### 3.3 Success Metrics

| Metric | Target | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Time idea to first watchable cut | days, not months | proves the loop closes |
| Project completion rate | > 40% of started projects | the real product test |
| Continuity defects per 100 shots | < 3 | quality differentiator |
| Asset reuse across a franchise | > 60% | proves the graph works |
| Normalized cost per finished minute | declining quarter over quarter | commercial viability |
| Approval turnaround | < 24h median | workflow credibility |

---

## 4. Architecture Principles

1. **One creative graph.** All studios read and write one project, universe, and asset graph.
2. **Studios are modules.** Registration is declarative; capabilities declare inputs, outputs, and schemas.
3. **No silent overwrite.** Approved artifacts require a new version and an approval event.
4. **Generation is a layer.** Model providers are interchangeable behind a single interface.
5. **Agents are employees.** Each has a role, tool scopes, a budget, and an audit trail.
6. **Human gates by default.** Consequential transitions require explicit approval.
7. **Continuity is computed.** Character, world, camera, sound, and narrative consistency are checked continuously.
8. **Everything is an asset.** Stable IDs, versions, provenance, rights, and dependencies.
9. **Cost is a first-class constraint.** Every job records credits and estimates before execution.
10. **Deletion is archival.** Nothing leaves the graph without an audit event.

---

## 5. Domain Model and Creative Graph

The graph connects universes to franchises to productions to scenes to shots to assets. Every edge is typed, versioned, and auditable.

```
UNIVERSE -> FRANCHISE -> [FILM | SERIES -> SEASON -> EPISODE]
                                      -> SCENE -> SHOT -> ASSET_VERSION
```

Core invariants:

- A shot cannot reference a character version that is not approved for its project.
- A location cannot be used in a scene after its continuity status is flagged unresolved.
- A cut cannot exceed a picture lock without creating a new edit version.
- A delivery master must reference a locked cut and a valid delivery profile.

---

## 6. Studio Family Specifications

Each capability below is specified to implementation depth: purpose, inputs, outputs, data contract, UX, agent protocol, pipeline, consistency rules, rights, performance, failure recovery, acceptance criteria, tests, telemetry, dependencies, and open questions.


## 6.1 STU-01 — Idea & Development Studio

**Phase:** P1 · **Sub-studios:** 4 · **Capabilities:** 33

**Mission.** Turn incomplete thoughts into developed, defensible creative concepts before a single frame is produced.

**Sub-studios.**
- Idea Studio
- Research Studio
- Creative Development Studio
- Production Packaging Studio

**Studio contract.** Every sub-studio exposes Overview, Workspace, Assets, Tools, Agents, References, Workflow, Tasks, Versions, Reviews, Approvals, History, and Export. Tabs that do not apply to the discipline are hidden rather than stubbed.

**Shared dependencies.** Project graph, asset store, agent registry, provider router, approval service, audit log, cost ledger.


### CAP-0001 — Idea capture

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Studio family | STU-01 Idea & Development Studio |
| Sub-studio | Idea Studio |
| Capability key | `idea-capture` |
| Phase / maturity | P1 / GA |
| Owner agent | AGT-01-01 · Idea Specialist |
| Requires approval | yes |

#### Purpose

Enable idea capture as a first-class production step inside Idea & Development Studio, so the result is versioned, reviewable, and reusable rather than trapped in a chat transcript.

The capability exists because turn incomplete thoughts into developed, defensible creative concepts before a single frame is produced. Without it, the department either stalls or exports work that downstream studios cannot consume.

#### Inputs and Outputs

- **In:** Approved project brief and creative constraints
- **In:** Locked upstream artifacts referenced by stable asset IDs
- **In:** Reference library items scoped to the current project
- **Out:** Review-ready proposal with rationale and provenance
- **Out:** Structured asset record with dependencies and rights metadata
- **Out:** Machine-readable spec consumed by downstream studios

#### Data Contract

```json
{ "capability": "idea-capture", "artifact_id": "art_...", "version": 1,
  "status": "approved", "agent": "AGT-01-01",
  "inputs": ["..."], "output": "idea-capture.result",
  "provenance": { "provider": "...", "model": "...", "seed": 1000 },
  "cost_credits": 1 }
```

#### UX Surface

- Split workspace: intent panel on the left, live artifact canvas on the right
- Inline diff view comparing the current proposal against the last approved version
- Traceability drawer showing every upstream artifact used in this result
- Command-palette invocation as `idea-capture`; every run is visible in the studio timeline with cost and duration.

#### Agent Protocol

1. **Plan.** Idea Specialist restates the objective, lists the upstream artifacts it will read, and estimates cost.
2. **Act.** Execute with capability-scoped tools, never writing outside the declared output schema; pause for human approval above the auto-approve threshold.
3. **Validate.** Schema validation plus the capability's acceptance tests before publish.
4. **Publish and hand off.** Commit the version with provenance, emit telemetry, and notify downstream owners with a diff summary.

#### Processing Pipeline

1. Resolve and validate inputs.
2. Construct the execution plan.
3. Generate or compute the artifact.
4. Score, self-review, and flag deviations.
5. Commit version and notify downstream.

#### Rules, Rights, and Recovery

- Reads resolve to approved versions only; drafts require explicit opt-in.
- Referenced characters, locations, and props must carry their asset IDs.
- Re-running never mutates a prior version; deviations from the visual or narrative bible are flagged.
- Only consented likenesses, voices, and licensed references may be used
- Every generated asset records provider, model version, and terms snapshot
- Upstream artifact missing or unapproved: block execution and deep-link to the blocking studio
- Provider timeout: retry with backoff, then fall back to the next authorized provider
- Low-confidence result: return three ranked alternatives instead of one answer

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-CAP-0001-1: a valid project yields a schema-valid `idea-capture` artifact with a stable ID.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0001-2: changed parameters create version 2 and leave version 1 retrievable.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0001-3: provenance exposes every upstream input, and unapproved artifacts are blocked downstream.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0001-4: cost and latency are recorded and visible in the studio timeline.

#### Test Cases and Telemetry

- TC-CAP-0001-1: Happy path returns a schema-valid artifact and a stable ID
- TC-CAP-0001-2: Rejected inputs surface actionable validation messages
- TC-CAP-0001-3: Duplicate runs are idempotent and do not create duplicate assets
- capability.invoked with project, studio, and agent identifiers
- capability.completed with latency, cost, and artifact version

#### Dependencies

- Phase gate P1; hard dependency on project graph service.
- Soft dependency on reference library.

#### Field Schema

| Field | Type | Required | Constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capability` | enum | yes | must equal `idea-capture` |
| `artifact_id` | uuid | yes | stable, never reused |
| `version` | integer | yes | monotonically increasing per artifact |
| `status` | enum | yes | proposed, in_review, approved, superseded |
| `inputs[]` | uuid[] | yes | approved versions only |
| `provenance` | jsonb | yes | agent, provider, model, seed recorded |
| `cost_credits` | integer | yes | written to the cost ledger |

**Open question.** Which provider set is authorized for this project's territory?

#### Edge Cases

- Empty upstream set: return a guided minimum-input checklist, never a fabricated artifact.
- Conflicting approved inputs: halt and present both records with their approval timestamps.
- Partially failed batch: keep successful items, mark the batch partial, and allow targeted retry.
- Oversized input: chunk by scene or asset and preserve a single provenance chain.
- Duplicate invocation within the idempotency window: return the existing run instead of charging again.

#### AI-Readable Contract

```yaml
capability: idea-capture
studio: STU-01
phase: P1
inputs: [artifact_id, params]
outputs: [artifact_id, version, status]
requires_approval: true
downstream: [idea-development-studio-consumers]
```

#### Observability

- Every run emits structured logs with run ID, capability key, and provider.
- Latency is broken down by stage so regressions are attributable.
- Cost is attributed to project, studio, capability, and agent.
- Failure classes are normalized across providers for comparable dashboards.

#### Rollout

- Ships behind a capability flag per project tier.
- Canary at 5% of eligible projects, then 25%, then general availability.
- Rollback disables the capability without deleting produced artifacts.
- Migration of existing artifacts is forward-only and audited.

#### Worked Example

- **Input.** A project with locked upstream artifacts and a clear creative intent for idea capture.
- **Run.** Idea Specialist resolves the graph, proposes a plan with cost, and executes after the gate.
- **Review.** The owner compares the proposal against the last approved version and accepts with notes.
- **Result.** A new version lands, downstream studios are notified, and the run is fully attributable.

#### Integration Points

- Reads from graph service.
- Writes through asset service.
- Emits events consumed by continuity engine.

2. **Act.** Execute with capability-scoped tools, never writing outside the declared output schema; pause for human approval above the auto-approve threshold.
3. **Validate.** Schema validation plus the capability's acceptance tests before publish.
4. **Publish and hand off.** Commit the version with provenance, emit telemetry, and notify downstream owners with a diff summary.

#### Processing Pipeline

1. Resolve and validate inputs.
2. Construct the execution plan.
3. Generate or compute the artifact.
4. Score, self-review, and flag deviations.
5. Commit version and notify downstream.

#### Rules, Rights, and Recovery

- Reads resolve to approved versions only; drafts require explicit opt-in.
- Referenced characters, locations, and props must carry their asset IDs.
- Re-running never mutates a prior version; deviations from the visual or narrative bible are flagged.
- Third-party references are stored as links, never redistributed
- Only consented likenesses, voices, and licensed references may be used
- Rights conflict detected: halt and surface the conflicting asset record
- Cost ceiling reached: stop the job, preserve partial output, request budget approval
- Upstream artifact missing or unapproved: block execution and deep-link to the blocking studio

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-CAP-0004-1: a valid project yields a schema-valid `image-to-concept-interpretation` artifact with a stable ID.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0004-2: changed parameters create version 2 and leave version 1 retrievable.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0004-3: provenance exposes every upstream input, and unapproved artifacts are blocked downstream.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0004-4: cost and latency are recorded and visible in the studio timeline.

#### Test Cases and Telemetry

- TC-CAP-0004-1: Downstream consumers can resolve the artifact without manual mapping
- TC-CAP-0004-2: Permission-denied requests are audited and produce no side effects
- TC-CAP-0004-3: Happy path returns a schema-valid artifact and a stable ID
- review.outcome with reviewer, decision, and dwell time
- capability.invoked with project, studio, and agent identifiers

#### Dependencies

- Phase gate P1; hard dependency on provider router.
- Soft dependency on cost ledger.

#### Field Schema

| Field | Type | Required | Constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capability` | enum | yes | must equal `image-to-concept-interpretation` |
| `artifact_id` | uuid | yes | stable, never reused |
| `version` | integer | yes | monotonically increasing per artifact |
| `status` | enum | yes | proposed, in_review, approved, superseded |
| `inputs[]` | uuid[] | yes | approved versions only |
| `provenance` | jsonb | yes | agent, provider, model, seed recorded |
| `cost_credits` | integer | yes | written to the cost ledger |

**Open question.** Which provider set is authorized for this project's territory?

#### Edge Cases

- Empty upstream set: return a guided minimum-input checklist, never a fabricated artifact.
- Conflicting approved inputs: halt and present both records with their approval timestamps.
- Partially failed batch: keep successful items, mark the batch partial, and allow targeted retry.
- Oversized input: chunk by scene or asset and preserve a single provenance chain.
- Duplicate invocation within the idempotency window: return the existing run instead of charging again.

#### AI-Readable Contract

```yaml
capability: image-to-concept-interpretation
studio: STU-01
phase: P1
inputs: [artifact_id, params]
outputs: [artifact_id, version, status]
requires_approval: true
downstream: [idea-development-studio-consumers]
```

#### Observability

- Every run emits structured logs with run ID, capability key, and provider.
- Latency is broken down by stage so regressions are attributable.
- Cost is attributed to project, studio, capability, and agent.
- Failure classes are normalized across providers for comparable dashboards.

#### Rollout

- Ships behind a capability flag per project tier.
- Canary at 5% of eligible projects, then 25%, then general availability.
- Rollback disables the capability without deleting produced artifacts.
- Migration of existing artifacts is forward-only and audited.

#### Worked Example

- **Input.** A project with locked upstream artifacts and a clear creative intent for image-to-concept interpretation.
- **Run.** Production Packaging Architect resolves the graph, proposes a plan with cost, and executes after the gate.
- **Review.** The owner compares the proposal against the last approved version and accepts with notes.
- **Result.** A new version lands, downstream studios are notified, and the run is fully attributable.

#### Integration Points

- Reads from canon service.
- Writes through artifact service.
- Emits events consumed by search index.

| Capability key | `originality-analysis` |
| Phase / maturity | P1 / GA |
| Owner agent | AGT-01-01 · Idea Specialist |
| Requires approval | no |

#### Purpose

Turn originality analysis from an ad-hoc prompt into a repeatable pipeline stage that a producer can budget and a reviewer can approve.

The capability exists because turn incomplete thoughts into developed, defensible creative concepts before a single frame is produced. Without it, the department either stalls or exports work that downstream studios cannot consume.

#### Inputs and Outputs

- **In:** Reference library items scoped to the current project
- **In:** Character, world, and location records resolved from the project graph
- **In:** Director intent notes and visual language bible
- **Out:** Human-readable summary surfaced in the studio workspace
- **Out:** Versioned creative artifact written back to the project graph
- **Out:** Review-ready proposal with rationale and provenance

#### Data Contract

```json
{ "capability": "originality-analysis", "artifact_id": "art_...", "version": 1,
  "status": "approved", "agent": "AGT-01-01",
  "inputs": ["..."], "output": "originality-analysis.result",
  "provenance": { "provider": "...", "model": "...", "seed": 1008 },
  "cost_credits": 9 }
```

#### UX Surface

- One-click accept, reject, or fork into a new branch
- Bottom timeline of runs with cost, duration, model, and outcome
- Split workspace: intent panel on the left, live artifact canvas on the right
- Command-palette invocation as `originality-analysis`; every run is visible in the studio timeline with cost and duration.

#### Agent Protocol

1. **Plan.** Idea Specialist restates the objective, lists the upstream artifacts it will read, and estimates cost.
2. **Act.** Execute with capability-scoped tools, never writing outside the declared output schema; pause for human approval above the auto-approve threshold.
3. **Validate.** Schema validation plus the capability's acceptance tests before publish.
4. **Publish and hand off.** Commit the version with provenance, emit telemetry, and notify downstream owners with a diff summary.

#### Processing Pipeline

1. Resolve and validate inputs.
2. Construct the execution plan.
3. Generate or compute the artifact.
4. Score, self-review, and flag deviations.
5. Commit version and notify downstream.

#### Rules, Rights, and Recovery

- Reads resolve to approved versions only; drafts require explicit opt-in.
- Referenced characters, locations, and props must carry their asset IDs.
- Re-running never mutates a prior version; deviations from the visual or narrative bible are flagged.
- Only consented likenesses, voices, and licensed references may be used
- Every generated asset records provider, model version, and terms snapshot
- Rights conflict detected: halt and surface the conflicting asset record
- Cost ceiling reached: stop the job, preserve partial output, request budget approval
- Upstream artifact missing or unapproved: block execution and deep-link to the blocking studio

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-CAP-0009-1: a valid project yields a schema-valid `originality-analysis` artifact with a stable ID.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0009-2: changed parameters create version 2 and leave version 1 retrievable.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0009-3: provenance exposes every upstream input, and unapproved artifacts are blocked downstream.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0009-4: cost and latency are recorded and visible in the studio timeline.

#### Test Cases and Telemetry

- TC-CAP-0009-1: Downstream consumers can resolve the artifact without manual mapping
- TC-CAP-0009-2: Permission-denied requests are audited and produce no side effects
- TC-CAP-0009-3: Happy path returns a schema-valid artifact and a stable ID
- capability.invoked with project, studio, and agent identifiers
- capability.completed with latency, cost, and artifact version

#### Dependencies

- Phase gate P1; hard dependency on project graph service.
- Soft dependency on reference library.

#### Field Schema

| Field | Type | Required | Constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capability` | enum | yes | must equal `originality-analysis` |
| `artifact_id` | uuid | yes | stable, never reused |
| `version` | integer | yes | monotonically increasing per artifact |
| `status` | enum | yes | proposed, in_review, approved, superseded |
| `inputs[]` | uuid[] | yes | approved versions only |
| `provenance` | jsonb | yes | agent, provider, model, seed recorded |
| `cost_credits` | integer | yes | written to the cost ledger |

**Open question.** What is the acceptable cost ceiling per invocation at scale?

#### Edge Cases

- Empty upstream set: return a guided minimum-input checklist, never a fabricated artifact.
- Conflicting approved inputs: halt and present both records with their approval timestamps.
- Partially failed batch: keep successful items, mark the batch partial, and allow targeted retry.
- Oversized input: chunk by scene or asset and preserve a single provenance chain.
- Duplicate invocation within the idempotency window: return the existing run instead of charging again.

#### AI-Readable Contract

```yaml
capability: originality-analysis
studio: STU-01
phase: P1
inputs: [artifact_id, params]
outputs: [artifact_id, version, status]
requires_approval: false
downstream: [idea-development-studio-consumers]
```

#### Observability

- Every run emits structured logs with run ID, capability key, and provider.
- Latency is broken down by stage so regressions are attributable.
- Cost is attributed to project, studio, capability, and agent.
- Failure classes are normalized across providers for comparable dashboards.

#### Rollout

- Ships behind a capability flag per project tier.
- Canary at 5% of eligible projects, then 25%, then general availability.
- Rollback disables the capability without deleting produced artifacts.
- Migration of existing artifacts is forward-only and audited.

#### Worked Example

- **Input.** A project with locked upstream artifacts and a clear creative intent for originality analysis.
- **Run.** Idea Specialist resolves the graph, proposes a plan with cost, and executes after the gate.
- **Review.** The owner compares the proposal against the last approved version and accepts with notes.
- **Result.** A new version lands, downstream studios are notified, and the run is fully attributable.

#### Integration Points

- Reads from graph service.
- Writes through asset service.
- Emits events consumed by continuity engine.

- [ ] AC-CAP-0018-2: changed parameters create version 2 and leave version 1 retrievable.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0018-3: provenance exposes every upstream input, and unapproved artifacts are blocked downstream.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0018-4: cost and latency are recorded and visible in the studio timeline.

#### Test Cases and Telemetry

- TC-CAP-0018-1: Duplicate runs are idempotent and do not create duplicate assets
- TC-CAP-0018-2: Downstream consumers can resolve the artifact without manual mapping
- TC-CAP-0018-3: Permission-denied requests are audited and produce no side effects
- capability.completed with latency, cost, and artifact version
- capability.failed with normalized error class and provider

#### Dependencies

- Phase gate P1; hard dependency on asset store and versioning.
- Soft dependency on search index.

#### Field Schema

| Field | Type | Required | Constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capability` | enum | yes | must equal `scientific-research` |
| `artifact_id` | uuid | yes | stable, never reused |
| `version` | integer | yes | monotonically increasing per artifact |
| `status` | enum | yes | proposed, in_review, approved, superseded |
| `inputs[]` | uuid[] | yes | approved versions only |
| `provenance` | jsonb | yes | agent, provider, model, seed recorded |
| `cost_credits` | integer | yes | written to the cost ledger |

**Open question.** What is the acceptable cost ceiling per invocation at scale?

#### Edge Cases

- Empty upstream set: return a guided minimum-input checklist, never a fabricated artifact.
- Conflicting approved inputs: halt and present both records with their approval timestamps.
- Partially failed batch: keep successful items, mark the batch partial, and allow targeted retry.
- Oversized input: chunk by scene or asset and preserve a single provenance chain.
- Duplicate invocation within the idempotency window: return the existing run instead of charging again.

#### AI-Readable Contract

```yaml
capability: scientific-research
studio: STU-01
phase: P1
inputs: [artifact_id, params]
outputs: [artifact_id, version, status]
requires_approval: false
downstream: [idea-development-studio-consumers]
```

#### Observability

- Every run emits structured logs with run ID, capability key, and provider.
- Latency is broken down by stage so regressions are attributable.
- Cost is attributed to project, studio, capability, and agent.
- Failure classes are normalized across providers for comparable dashboards.

#### Rollout

- Ships behind a capability flag per project tier.
- Canary at 5% of eligible projects, then 25%, then general availability.
- Rollback disables the capability without deleting produced artifacts.
- Migration of existing artifacts is forward-only and audited.

#### Worked Example

- **Input.** A project with locked upstream artifacts and a clear creative intent for scientific research.
- **Run.** Research Supervisor resolves the graph, proposes a plan with cost, and executes after the gate.
- **Review.** The owner compares the proposal against the last approved version and accepts with notes.
- **Result.** A new version lands, downstream studios are notified, and the run is fully attributable.

#### Integration Points

- Reads from artifact service.
- Writes through approval service.
- Emits events consumed by cost ledger.

```json
  "provenance": { "provider": "...", "model": "...", "seed": 1022 },
  "cost_credits": 5 }
```

#### UX Surface

- Traceability drawer showing every upstream artifact used in this result
- One-click accept, reject, or fork into a new branch
- Bottom timeline of runs with cost, duration, model, and outcome
- Command-palette invocation as `source-verification-and-fact-checking`; every run is visible in the studio timeline with cost and duration.

#### Agent Protocol

1. **Plan.** Creative Development Director restates the objective, lists the upstream artifacts it will read, and estimates cost.
2. **Act.** Execute with capability-scoped tools, never writing outside the declared output schema; pause for human approval above the auto-approve threshold.
3. **Validate.** Schema validation plus the capability's acceptance tests before publish.
4. **Publish and hand off.** Commit the version with provenance, emit telemetry, and notify downstream owners with a diff summary.

#### Processing Pipeline

1. Resolve and validate inputs.
2. Construct the execution plan.
3. Generate or compute the artifact.
4. Score, self-review, and flag deviations.
5. Commit version and notify downstream.

#### Rules, Rights, and Recovery

- Reads resolve to approved versions only; drafts require explicit opt-in.
- Referenced characters, locations, and props must carry their asset IDs.
- Re-running never mutates a prior version; deviations from the visual or narrative bible are flagged.
- No training or fine-tuning on user IP without explicit written consent
- Third-party references are stored as links, never redistributed
- Low-confidence result: return three ranked alternatives instead of one answer
- Rights conflict detected: halt and surface the conflicting asset record
- Cost ceiling reached: stop the job, preserve partial output, request budget approval

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-CAP-0023-1: a valid project yields a schema-valid `source-verification-and-fact-checking` artifact with a stable ID.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0023-2: changed parameters create version 2 and leave version 1 retrievable.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0023-3: provenance exposes every upstream input, and unapproved artifacts are blocked downstream.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0023-4: cost and latency are recorded and visible in the studio timeline.

#### Test Cases and Telemetry

- TC-CAP-0023-1: Duplicate runs are idempotent and do not create duplicate assets
- TC-CAP-0023-2: Downstream consumers can resolve the artifact without manual mapping
- TC-CAP-0023-3: Permission-denied requests are audited and produce no side effects
- capability.failed with normalized error class and provider
- review.outcome with reviewer, decision, and dwell time

#### Dependencies

- Phase gate P1; hard dependency on approval service.
- Soft dependency on continuity engine.

#### Field Schema

| Field | Type | Required | Constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capability` | enum | yes | must equal `source-verification-and-fact-checking` |
| `artifact_id` | uuid | yes | stable, never reused |
| `version` | integer | yes | monotonically increasing per artifact |
| `status` | enum | yes | proposed, in_review, approved, superseded |
| `inputs[]` | uuid[] | yes | approved versions only |
| `provenance` | jsonb | yes | agent, provider, model, seed recorded |
| `cost_credits` | integer | yes | written to the cost ledger |

**Open question.** Does this capability require a human approval gate before downstream use?

#### Edge Cases

- Empty upstream set: return a guided minimum-input checklist, never a fabricated artifact.
- Conflicting approved inputs: halt and present both records with their approval timestamps.
- Partially failed batch: keep successful items, mark the batch partial, and allow targeted retry.
- Oversized input: chunk by scene or asset and preserve a single provenance chain.
- Duplicate invocation within the idempotency window: return the existing run instead of charging again.

#### AI-Readable Contract

```yaml
capability: source-verification-and-fact-checking
studio: STU-01
phase: P1
inputs: [artifact_id, params]
outputs: [artifact_id, version, status]
requires_approval: false
downstream: [idea-development-studio-consumers]
```

#### Observability

- Every run emits structured logs with run ID, capability key, and provider.
- Latency is broken down by stage so regressions are attributable.
- Cost is attributed to project, studio, capability, and agent.
- Failure classes are normalized across providers for comparable dashboards.

#### Rollout

- Ships behind a capability flag per project tier.
- Canary at 5% of eligible projects, then 25%, then general availability.
- Rollback disables the capability without deleting produced artifacts.
- Migration of existing artifacts is forward-only and audited.

#### Worked Example

- **Input.** A project with locked upstream artifacts and a clear creative intent for source verification and fact-checking.
- **Run.** Creative Development Director resolves the graph, proposes a plan with cost, and executes after the gate.
- **Review.** The owner compares the proposal against the last approved version and accepts with notes.
- **Result.** A new version lands, downstream studios are notified, and the run is fully attributable.

#### Integration Points

- Reads from asset service.
- Writes through export service.
- Emits events consumed by workflow orchestrator.

| `version` | integer | yes | monotonically increasing per artifact |
| `status` | enum | yes | proposed, in_review, approved, superseded |
| `inputs[]` | uuid[] | yes | approved versions only |
| `provenance` | jsonb | yes | agent, provider, model, seed recorded |
| `cost_credits` | integer | yes | written to the cost ledger |

**Open question.** Does this capability require a human approval gate before downstream use?

#### Edge Cases

- Empty upstream set: return a guided minimum-input checklist, never a fabricated artifact.
- Conflicting approved inputs: halt and present both records with their approval timestamps.
- Partially failed batch: keep successful items, mark the batch partial, and allow targeted retry.
- Oversized input: chunk by scene or asset and preserve a single provenance chain.
- Duplicate invocation within the idempotency window: return the existing run instead of charging again.

#### AI-Readable Contract

```yaml
capability: director-s-statement
studio: STU-01
phase: P1
inputs: [artifact_id, params]
outputs: [artifact_id, version, status]
requires_approval: false
downstream: [idea-development-studio-consumers]
```

#### Observability

- Every run emits structured logs with run ID, capability key, and provider.
- Latency is broken down by stage so regressions are attributable.
- Cost is attributed to project, studio, capability, and agent.
- Failure classes are normalized across providers for comparable dashboards.

#### Rollout

- Ships behind a capability flag per project tier.
- Canary at 5% of eligible projects, then 25%, then general availability.
- Rollback disables the capability without deleting produced artifacts.
- Migration of existing artifacts is forward-only and audited.

#### Worked Example

- **Input.** A project with locked upstream artifacts and a clear creative intent for director's statement.
- **Run.** Production Packaging Auditor resolves the graph, proposes a plan with cost, and executes after the gate.
- **Review.** The owner compares the proposal against the last approved version and accepts with notes.
- **Result.** A new version lands, downstream studios are notified, and the run is fully attributable.

#### Integration Points

- Reads from canon service.
- Writes through artifact service.
- Emits events consumed by search index.

#### Agent Protocol

1. **Plan.** Series Architecture Architect restates the objective, lists the upstream artifacts it will read, and estimates cost.
2. **Act.** Execute with capability-scoped tools, never writing outside the declared output schema; pause for human approval above the auto-approve threshold.
3. **Validate.** Schema validation plus the capability's acceptance tests before publish.
4. **Publish and hand off.** Commit the version with provenance, emit telemetry, and notify downstream owners with a diff summary.

#### Processing Pipeline

1. Resolve and validate inputs.
2. Construct the execution plan.
3. Generate or compute the artifact.
4. Score, self-review, and flag deviations.
5. Commit version and notify downstream.

#### Rules, Rights, and Recovery

- Reads resolve to approved versions only; drafts require explicit opt-in.
- Referenced characters, locations, and props must carry their asset IDs.
- Re-running never mutates a prior version; deviations from the visual or narrative bible are flagged.
- Third-party references are stored as links, never redistributed
- Only consented likenesses, voices, and licensed references may be used
- Rights conflict detected: halt and surface the conflicting asset record
- Cost ceiling reached: stop the job, preserve partial output, request budget approval
- Upstream artifact missing or unapproved: block execution and deep-link to the blocking studio

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-CAP-0037-1: a valid project yields a schema-valid `save-the-cat-beat-sheet` artifact with a stable ID.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0037-2: changed parameters create version 2 and leave version 1 retrievable.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0037-3: provenance exposes every upstream input, and unapproved artifacts are blocked downstream.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0037-4: cost and latency are recorded and visible in the studio timeline.

#### Test Cases and Telemetry

- TC-CAP-0037-1: Downstream consumers can resolve the artifact without manual mapping
- TC-CAP-0037-2: Permission-denied requests are audited and produce no side effects
- TC-CAP-0037-3: Happy path returns a schema-valid artifact and a stable ID
- review.outcome with reviewer, decision, and dwell time
- capability.invoked with project, studio, and agent identifiers

#### Dependencies

- Phase gate P1; hard dependency on provider router.
- Soft dependency on cost ledger.

#### Field Schema

| Field | Type | Required | Constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capability` | enum | yes | must equal `save-the-cat-beat-sheet` |
| `artifact_id` | uuid | yes | stable, never reused |
| `version` | integer | yes | monotonically increasing per artifact |
| `status` | enum | yes | proposed, in_review, approved, superseded |
| `inputs[]` | uuid[] | yes | approved versions only |
| `provenance` | jsonb | yes | agent, provider, model, seed recorded |
| `cost_credits` | integer | yes | written to the cost ledger |

**Open question.** Which provider set is authorized for this project's territory?

#### Edge Cases

- Empty upstream set: return a guided minimum-input checklist, never a fabricated artifact.
- Conflicting approved inputs: halt and present both records with their approval timestamps.
- Partially failed batch: keep successful items, mark the batch partial, and allow targeted retry.
- Oversized input: chunk by scene or asset and preserve a single provenance chain.
- Duplicate invocation within the idempotency window: return the existing run instead of charging again.

#### AI-Readable Contract

```yaml
capability: save-the-cat-beat-sheet
studio: STU-02
phase: P1

outputs: [artifact_id, version, status]
requires_approval: true
downstream: [story-architecture-studio-consumers]
```

#### Observability

- Every run emits structured logs with run ID, capability key, and provider.
- Latency is broken down by stage so regressions are attributable.
- Cost is attributed to project, studio, capability, and agent.
- Failure classes are normalized across providers for comparable dashboards.

#### Rollout

- Ships behind a capability flag per project tier.
- Canary at 5% of eligible projects, then 25%, then general availability.
- Rollback disables the capability without deleting produced artifacts.
- Migration of existing artifacts is forward-only and audited.

- **Input.** A project with locked upstream artifacts and a clear creative intent for save the cat beat sheet.

- **Review.** The owner compares the proposal against the last approved version and accepts with notes.
- **Result.** A new version lands, downstream studios are notified, and the run is fully attributable.

- Writes through artifact service.
- Emits events consumed by search index.

### CAP-0042 — Anthology structure

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Studio family | STU-02 Story Architecture Studio |
| Sub-studio | Structure Studio |
| Capability key | `anthology-structure` |
| Phase / maturity | P1 / GA |
| Owner agent | AGT-02-01 · Structure Specialist |
| Requires approval | no |

#### Purpose

Turn anthology structure from an ad-hoc prompt into a repeatable pipeline stage that a producer can budget and a reviewer can approve.

The capability exists because give every project a structural spine that survives rewriting, expansion, and serialization. Without it, the department either stalls or exports work that downstream studios cannot consume.

#### Inputs and Outputs

- **In:** Reference library items scoped to the current project
- **In:** Character, world, and location records resolved from the project graph
- **In:** Director intent notes and visual language bible
- **Out:** Human-readable summary surfaced in the studio workspace
- **Out:** Versioned creative artifact written back to the project graph
- **Out:** Review-ready proposal with rationale and provenance

#### Data Contract

```json
{ "capability": "anthology-structure", "artifact_id": "art_...", "version": 1,
  "status": "approved", "agent": "AGT-02-01",
  "inputs": ["..."], "output": "anthology-structure.result",
  "provenance": { "provider": "...", "model": "...", "seed": 1008 },
  "cost_credits": 9 }
```

#### UX Surface

- One-click accept, reject, or fork into a new branch
- Bottom timeline of runs with cost, duration, model, and outcome
- Split workspace: intent panel on the left, live artifact canvas on the right
- Command-palette invocation as `anthology-structure`; every run is visible in the studio timeline with cost and duration.

#### Agent Protocol

1. **Plan.** Structure Specialist restates the objective, lists the upstream artifacts it will read, and estimates cost.
2. **Act.** Execute with capability-scoped tools, never writing outside the declared output schema; pause for human approval above the auto-approve threshold.
3. **Validate.** Schema validation plus the capability's acceptance tests before publish.
4. **Publish and hand off.** Commit the version with provenance, emit telemetry, and notify downstream owners with a diff summary.

#### Processing Pipeline

1. Resolve and validate inputs.
2. Construct the execution plan.
3. Generate or compute the artifact.
4. Score, self-review, and flag deviations.
5. Commit version and notify downstream.

#### Rules, Rights, and Recovery

- Reads resolve to approved versions only; drafts require explicit opt-in.
- Referenced characters, locations, and props must carry their asset IDs.
- Re-running never mutates a prior version; deviations from the visual or narrative bible are flagged.
- Only consented likenesses, voices, and licensed references may be used
- Every generated asset records provider, model version, and terms snapshot
- Rights conflict detected: halt and surface the conflicting asset record
- Cost ceiling reached: stop the job, preserve partial output, request budget approval
- Upstream artifact missing or unapproved: block execution and deep-link to the blocking studio

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-CAP-0042-1: a valid project yields a schema-valid `anthology-structure` artifact with a stable ID.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0042-2: changed parameters create version 2 and leave version 1 retrievable.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0042-3: provenance exposes every upstream input, and unapproved artifacts are blocked downstream.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0042-4: cost and latency are recorded and visible in the studio timeline.

#### Test Cases and Telemetry

- TC-CAP-0042-1: Downstream consumers can resolve the artifact without manual mapping
- TC-CAP-0042-2: Permission-denied requests are audited and produce no side effects
- TC-CAP-0042-3: Happy path returns a schema-valid artifact and a stable ID
- capability.invoked with project, studio, and agent identifiers
- capability.completed with latency, cost, and artifact version

#### Dependencies

- Phase gate P1; hard dependency on project graph service.
- Soft dependency on reference library.

#### Field Schema

| Field | Type | Required | Constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capability` | enum | yes | must equal `anthology-structure` |
| `artifact_id` | uuid | yes | stable, never reused |
| `version` | integer | yes | monotonically increasing per artifact |
| `status` | enum | yes | proposed, in_review, approved, superseded |
| `inputs[]` | uuid[] | yes | approved versions only |
| `provenance` | jsonb | yes | agent, provider, model, seed recorded |
| `cost_credits` | integer | yes | written to the cost ledger |

**Open question.** What is the acceptable cost ceiling per invocation at scale?

#### Edge Cases

- Empty upstream set: return a guided minimum-input checklist, never a fabricated artifact.
- Conflicting approved inputs: halt and present both records with their approval timestamps.
- Partially failed batch: keep successful items, mark the batch partial, and allow targeted retry.
- Oversized input: chunk by scene or asset and preserve a single provenance chain.
- Duplicate invocation within the idempotency window: return the existing run instead of charging again.

#### AI-Readable Contract

```yaml
capability: anthology-structure
studio: STU-02
phase: P1
inputs: [artifact_id, params]
outputs: [artifact_id, version, status]
requires_approval: false
downstream: [story-architecture-studio-consumers]
```

#### Observability

- Every run emits structured logs with run ID, capability key, and provider.
- Latency is broken down by stage so regressions are attributable.
- Cost is attributed to project, studio, capability, and agent.
- Failure classes are normalized across providers for comparable dashboards.

#### Rollout

- Ships behind a capability flag per project tier.
- Canary at 5% of eligible projects, then 25%, then general availability.
- Rollback disables the capability without deleting produced artifacts.
- Migration of existing artifacts is forward-only and audited.

#### Worked Example

- **Input.** A project with locked upstream artifacts and a clear creative intent for anthology structure.
- **Run.** Structure Specialist resolves the graph, proposes a plan with cost, and executes after the gate.
- **Review.** The owner compares the proposal against the last approved version and accepts with notes.
- **Result.** A new version lands, downstream studios are notified, and the run is fully attributable.

#### Integration Points

- Reads from graph service.
- Writes through asset service.
- Emits events consumed by continuity engine.

#### Edge Cases

- Oversized input: chunk by scene or asset and preserve a single provenance chain.
- Duplicate invocation within the idempotency window: return the existing run instead of charging again.

2. **Act.** Execute with capability-scoped tools, never writing outside the declared output schema; pause for human approval above the auto-approve threshold.
3. **Validate.** Schema validation plus the capability's acceptance tests before publish.
4. **Publish and hand off.** Commit the version with provenance, emit telemetry, and notify downstream owners with a diff summary.

#### Processing Pipeline

1. Resolve and validate inputs.
2. Construct the execution plan.
3. Generate or compute the artifact.
4. Score, self-review, and flag deviations.
5. Commit version and notify downstream.

#### Rules, Rights, and Recovery

- Reads resolve to approved versions only; drafts require explicit opt-in.
- Referenced characters, locations, and props must carry their asset IDs.
- Re-running never mutates a prior version; deviations from the visual or narrative bible are flagged.
- Every generated asset records provider, model version, and terms snapshot
- No training or fine-tuning on user IP without explicit written consent
- Provider timeout: retry with backoff, then fall back to the next authorized provider
- Low-confidence result: return three ranked alternatives instead of one answer
- Rights conflict detected: halt and surface the conflicting asset record

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-CAP-0051-1: a valid project yields a schema-valid `scene-writing` artifact with a stable ID.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0051-2: changed parameters create version 2 and leave version 1 retrievable.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0051-3: provenance exposes every upstream input, and unapproved artifacts are blocked downstream.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0051-4: cost and latency are recorded and visible in the studio timeline.

#### Test Cases and Telemetry

- TC-CAP-0051-1: Rejected inputs surface actionable validation messages
- TC-CAP-0051-2: Duplicate runs are idempotent and do not create duplicate assets
- TC-CAP-0051-3: Downstream consumers can resolve the artifact without manual mapping
- capability.completed with latency, cost, and artifact version
- capability.failed with normalized error class and provider

#### Dependencies

- Phase gate P1; hard dependency on asset store and versioning.
- Soft dependency on search index.

#### Field Schema

| Field | Type | Required | Constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capability` | enum | yes | must equal `scene-writing` |
| `artifact_id` | uuid | yes | stable, never reused |
| `version` | integer | yes | monotonically increasing per artifact |
| `status` | enum | yes | proposed, in_review, approved, superseded |
| `inputs[]` | uuid[] | yes | approved versions only |
| `provenance` | jsonb | yes | agent, provider, model, seed recorded |
| `cost_credits` | integer | yes | written to the cost ledger |

**Open question.** Does this capability require a human approval gate before downstream use?

#### Edge Cases

- Empty upstream set: return a guided minimum-input checklist, never a fabricated artifact.
- Conflicting approved inputs: halt and present both records with their approval timestamps.
- Partially failed batch: keep successful items, mark the batch partial, and allow targeted retry.
- Oversized input: chunk by scene or asset and preserve a single provenance chain.
- Duplicate invocation within the idempotency window: return the existing run instead of charging again.

#### AI-Readable Contract

```yaml
capability: scene-writing
studio: STU-03
phase: P1
inputs: [artifact_id, params]
outputs: [artifact_id, version, status]
requires_approval: false
downstream: [screenplay-studio-consumers]
```

#### Observability

- Every run emits structured logs with run ID, capability key, and provider.
- Latency is broken down by stage so regressions are attributable.
- Cost is attributed to project, studio, capability, and agent.
- Failure classes are normalized across providers for comparable dashboards.

#### Rollout

- Ships behind a capability flag per project tier.
- Canary at 5% of eligible projects, then 25%, then general availability.
- Rollback disables the capability without deleting produced artifacts.
- Migration of existing artifacts is forward-only and audited.

#### Worked Example

- **Input.** A project with locked upstream artifacts and a clear creative intent for scene writing.
- **Run.** Rewrite Supervisor resolves the graph, proposes a plan with cost, and executes after the gate.
- **Review.** The owner compares the proposal against the last approved version and accepts with notes.
- **Result.** A new version lands, downstream studios are notified, and the run is fully attributable.

#### Integration Points

- Reads from artifact service.
- Writes through approval service.
- Emits events consumed by cost ledger.

| Capability key | `screenplay-formatting` |
| Phase / maturity | P1 / GA |
| Owner agent | AGT-03-01 · Scene Writing Director |
| Requires approval | yes |

#### Purpose

Enable screenplay formatting as a first-class production step inside Screenplay Studio, so the result is versioned, reviewable, and reusable rather than trapped in a chat transcript.

The capability exists because write, format, version, and lock screenplays inside the same graph as characters, scenes, and shots. Without it, the department either stalls or exports work that downstream studios cannot consume.

#### Inputs and Outputs

- **In:** Approved project brief and creative constraints
- **In:** Locked upstream artifacts referenced by stable asset IDs
- **In:** Reference library items scoped to the current project
- **Out:** Structured asset record with dependencies and rights metadata
- **Out:** Machine-readable spec consumed by downstream studios
- **Out:** Human-readable summary surfaced in the studio workspace

#### Data Contract

```json
{ "capability": "screenplay-formatting", "artifact_id": "art_...", "version": 3,
  "status": "approved", "agent": "AGT-03-01",
  "inputs": ["..."], "output": "screenplay-formatting.result",
  "provenance": { "provider": "...", "model": "...", "seed": 1006 },
  "cost_credits": 7 }
```

#### UX Surface

- Inline diff view comparing the current proposal against the last approved version
- Traceability drawer showing every upstream artifact used in this result
- One-click accept, reject, or fork into a new branch
- Command-palette invocation as `screenplay-formatting`; every run is visible in the studio timeline with cost and duration.

#### Agent Protocol

1. **Plan.** Scene Writing Director restates the objective, lists the upstream artifacts it will read, and estimates cost.
2. **Act.** Execute with capability-scoped tools, never writing outside the declared output schema; pause for human approval above the auto-approve threshold.
3. **Validate.** Schema validation plus the capability's acceptance tests before publish.
4. **Publish and hand off.** Commit the version with provenance, emit telemetry, and notify downstream owners with a diff summary.

#### Processing Pipeline

1. Resolve and validate inputs.
2. Construct the execution plan.
3. Generate or compute the artifact.
4. Score, self-review, and flag deviations.
5. Commit version and notify downstream.

#### Rules, Rights, and Recovery

- Reads resolve to approved versions only; drafts require explicit opt-in.
- Referenced characters, locations, and props must carry their asset IDs.
- Re-running never mutates a prior version; deviations from the visual or narrative bible are flagged.
- No training or fine-tuning on user IP without explicit written consent
- Third-party references are stored as links, never redistributed
- Provider timeout: retry with backoff, then fall back to the next authorized provider
- Low-confidence result: return three ranked alternatives instead of one answer
- Rights conflict detected: halt and surface the conflicting asset record

#### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-CAP-0056-1: a valid project yields a schema-valid `screenplay-formatting` artifact with a stable ID.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0056-2: changed parameters create version 2 and leave version 1 retrievable.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0056-3: provenance exposes every upstream input, and unapproved artifacts are blocked downstream.
- [ ] AC-CAP-0056-4: cost and latency are recorded and visible in the studio timeline.

#### Test Cases and Telemetry

- TC-CAP-0056-1: Rejected inputs surface actionable validation messages
- TC-CAP-0056-2: Duplicate runs are idempotent and do not create duplicate assets
- TC-CAP-0056-3: Downstream consumers can resolve the artifact without manual mapping
- capability.failed with normalized error class and provider
- review.outcome with reviewer, decision, and dwell time

#### Dependencies

- Phase gate P1; hard dependency on approval service.
- Soft dependency on continuity engine.

#### Field Schema

| Field | Type | Required | Constraint |
|---|---|---|---|
| `capability` | enum | yes | must equal `screenplay-formatting` |
| `artifact_id` | uuid | yes | stable, never reused |
| `version` | integer | yes | monotonically increasing per artifact |
| `status` | enum | yes | proposed, in_review, approved, superseded |
| `inputs[]` | uuid[] | yes | approved versions only |
| `provenance` | jsonb | yes | agent, provider, model, seed recorded |
| `cost_credits` | integer | yes | written to the cost ledger |

**Open question.** Which provider set is authorized for this project's territory?

#### Edge Cases

- Empty upstream set: return a guided minimum-input checklist, never a fabricated artifact.
- Conflicting approved inputs: halt and present both records with their approval timestamps.
- Partially failed batch: keep successful items, mark the batch partial, and allow targeted retry.
- Oversized input: chunk by scene or asset and preserve a single provenance chain.
- Duplicate invocation within the idempotency window: return the existing run instead of charging again.

#### AI-Readable Contract

```yaml
capability: screenplay-formatting
studio: STU-03
phase: P1
inputs: [artifact_id, params]
outputs: [artifact_id, version, status]
requires_approval: true
downstream: [screenplay-studio-consumers]
```

#### Observability

- Every run emits structured logs with run ID, capability key, and provider.
- Latency is broken down by stage so regressions are attributable.
- Cost is attributed to project, studio, capability, and agent.
- Failure classes are normalized across providers for comparable dashboards.

#### Rollout

- Ships behind a capability flag per project tier.
- Canary at 5% of eligible projects, then 25%, then general availability.
- Rollback disables the capability without deleting produced artifacts.
- Migration of existing artifacts is forward-only and audited.

#### Worked Example

- **Input.** A project with locked upstream artifacts and a clear creative intent for screenplay formatting.
- **Run.** Scene Writing Director resolves the graph, proposes a plan with cost, and executes after the gate.
- **Review.** The owner compares the proposal against the last approved version and accepts with notes.
- **Result.** A new version lands, downstream studios are notified, and the run is fully attributable.

#### Integration Points

- Reads from asset service.
- Writes through export service.
- Emits events consumed by workflow orchestrator.

- Conflicting approved inputs: halt and present both records with their approval timestamps.
- Partially failed batch: keep successful items, mark the batch partial, and allow targeted retry.
- Oversized input: chunk by scene or asset and preserve a single provenance chain.
- Duplicate invocation within the idempotency window: return the existing run instead of charging again.

#### AI-Readable Contract

```yaml
capability: subtext-analysis
studio: STU-03
phase: P1
inputs: [artifact_id, params]
outputs: [artifact_id, version, status]
requires_approval: false
downstream: [screenplay-studio-consumers]
```

#### Observability

- Every run emits structured logs with run ID, capability key, and provider.
- Latency is broken down by stage so regressions are attributable.
- Cost is attributed to project, studio, capability, and agent.
- Failure classes are normalized across providers for comparable dashboards.

#### Rollout

- Ships behind a capability flag per project tier.
- Canary at 5% of eligible projects, then 25%, then general availability.
- Rollback disables the capability without deleting produced artifacts.
- Migration of existing artifacts is forward-only and audited.

#### Worked Example

- **Input.** A project with locked upstream artifacts and a clear creative intent for subtext analysis.
- **Run.** Scene Writing Coordinator resolves the graph, proposes a plan with cost, and executes after the gate.
- **Review.** The owner compares the proposal against the last approved version and accepts with notes.
- **Result.** A new version lands, downstream studios are notified, and the run is fully attributable.

#### Integration Points

- Reads from asset service.
- Writes through export service.
- Emits events consumed by workflow orchestrator.
