## 14. Film School: 150 Years of Craft Knowledge

### 14.1 Thesis

The academy inside CreativeOS compresses more than a century of accumulated craft into the exact moment a decision is being made. It is not a video course library bolted onto a tool. It is a teaching layer that explains, demonstrates, and drills the principles behind the artifact on screen.

The curriculum covers the full arc of moving-image craft: silent-era grammar, studio-system continuity, auteur cinematography, new-wave editing, blockbuster effects, digital color, and contemporary virtual production.

### 14.2 Knowledge Timeline

| Year | Knowledge milestone |
|---|---|
| 1888 | first motion-picture capture and the birth of the frame |
| 1895 | projection to a paying audience establishes cinema as a public form |
| 1902 | trick effects and substitution splices prove the frame can lie |
| 1915 | feature-length narrative grammar consolidates |
| 1920s | Soviet montage formalizes editing as meaning |
| 1927 | synchronized sound rewrites performance and staging |
| 1930s | studio-system continuity and the three-point lighting standard |
| 1940s | film noir codifies shadow, moral ambiguity, and low-key light |
| 1950s | widescreen formats change composition and scale |
| 1960s | new waves break continuity rules deliberately |
| 1970s | auteur era and the blockbuster model emerge together |
| 1977 | optical effects and sound design become a franchise engine |
| 1980s | analog compositing and motion-control mature |
| 1993 | digital compositing changes creature realism permanently |
| 1999 | digital intermediates make color a post-production discipline |
| 2000s | performance capture and digital doubles enter production |
| 2009 | stereoscopic and large-format pipelines scale |
| 2010s | virtual production and real-time engines enter the set |
| 2019 | LED volume photography normalizes in-camera VFX |
| 2020s | generative models enter previs, look development, and finishing |

### 14.4 Craft Knowledge Graph

- Concepts link to the capabilities that use them, so teaching is contextual.
- Each concept carries examples, counter-examples, and a measurable rubric.
- Mastery is tracked per concept and decays without practice.
- Explanations are localized and adapted to the user's demonstrated level.

### 14.5 Mentor Pedagogy

- Explain only when the user is about to make the decision.
- Show the principle on the user's own footage, not on stock examples.
- Offer one exercise, not a curriculum dump.
- Critique with specifics: what works, what fails, and the smallest fix.
- Never flatter; correctness over encouragement.

### 14.6 Practice and Certification

- Practice studio recreates reference shots and scenes with guided constraints.
- Assessments are artifact-based, not quiz-based.
- Certificates record demonstrated competence with a signed portfolio.
- Educators can assign modules and review submissions inside the same graph.

### 14.7 Source Provenance

- Every lesson cites its craft lineage and avoids unlicensed reproductions.
- Film references are described and analyzed, not redistributed.
- Corrections are versioned and attributed.
- The academy never teaches a technique whose rights posture is unclear.

## 15. System Design and Platform Architecture

### 15.1 Architecture Overview

```
CLIENT (web, mobile, tablet, desktop shell)
  -> EDGE (auth, rate limit, routing, regional pinning)
     -> API GATEWAY (capability router, idempotency, quotas)
        -> DOMAIN SERVICES (graph, artifacts, assets, IP, canon, approvals)
           -> ORCHESTRATOR (workflow DAG, gates, retries)
              -> JOB QUEUE (priority classes, provider lanes)
                 -> PROVIDER ROUTER (model and tool abstraction)
                    -> WORKERS (generation, analysis, QC, media ops)
                       -> STORAGE (object, relational, vector, timeline)
```

### 15.2 Service Catalogue

| Service | Responsibility | Failure isolation |
|---|---|---|
| Identity Service | authentication, sessions, device trust | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Tenant Service | organizations, seats, hierarchies | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Project Service | projects, universes, franchises, titles | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Graph Service | typed edges, invariants, traversal | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Artifact Service | versioned creative artifacts and diffs | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Asset Service | typed assets, versions, dependencies | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Rights Service | licenses, consent, attribution | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Canon Service | canon status, conflict resolution | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Approval Service | gates, routing, decisions, audit | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Workflow Service | DAG definitions and execution state | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Job Service | queues, retries, idempotency, priorities | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Provider Router | model and tool selection and fallback | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Generation Gateway | normalized image, video, audio, text calls | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Media Service | transcode, proxy, conform, delivery | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Timeline Service | edit model for scenes and sequences | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Review Service | timecoded notes, threads, resolutions | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Search Service | hybrid lexical, vector, and graph search | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Notification Service | consequential updates only | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Companion Service | Bella state, memory, proactivity policy | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Learning Service | modules, drills, assessments, progress | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Telemetry Service | events, metrics, traces | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Cost Service | metering, ledgers, budgets, forecasts | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Billing Service | plans, credits, invoices, entitlements | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Export Service | format targets and validation | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |
| Delivery Service | masters, profiles, handoff records | independent deploy, degraded-mode contract |

### 15.3 Request Lifecycle

1. Edge authenticates, resolves tenant and region, and attaches a trace ID.
2. Gateway resolves the capability, checks entitlements, credits, and idempotency key.
3. Domain service validates inputs against the artifact schema and approval state.
4. Orchestrator expands the workflow DAG and enqueues jobs by priority class.
5. Provider router selects an authorized provider and records the choice.
6. Workers execute, stream stage events, and write artifacts transactionally.
7. Approval service records the gate; downstream is notified only after commit.

### 15.4 Storage Model

- **Relational:** entities, versions, approvals, entitlements, ledgers.
- **Object:** media, masters, plates, stems, exports, with immutable versioning.
- **Vector:** references, embeddings, similarity search across assets.
- **Graph:** canon edges, dependencies, lineage, and cross-project reuse.
- **Time-series:** cost, latency, quality, and usage metrics.
- **Event log:** append-only audit and provenance stream.

### 15.5 Queue Design

| Class | Latency target | Examples | Preemption |
|---|---|---|---|
| interactive | < 2s | companion reads, schema validation | never |
| session | < 30s | image drafts, panel generation | after 2 min |
| production | minutes to hours | video shots, simulations | after 30 min |
| batch | hours | upscales, conforms, exports | yes |

- Per-tenant concurrency caps prevent noisy-neighbor starvation.
- Jobs are idempotent and resumable with checkpointed stage state.
- Dead-letter queues feed a repair console with replay.

### 15.6 Provider Abstraction

- One normalized interface per media type with capability declarations.
- Providers declare limits: resolution, duration, safety filters, pricing.
- Router scores providers by quality prediction, cost, and availability.
- Failover preserves the shot spec so a re-render is comparable.
- Model versions are pinned per approved artifact for reproducibility.

### 15.7 Multi-Tenancy and Permissions

- Row-level isolation by tenant and project with region pinning.
- Roles: owner, producer, department lead, artist, reviewer, viewer, auditor.
- Permissions are capability-scoped, not screen-scoped.
- Studio-level and asset-level sharing with explicit grants.
- Every permission change is audited with actor and reason.

### 15.8 Security and Privacy

- Encryption in transit and at rest; per-tenant keys for sensitive media.
- Signed URLs for media access with short expiry.
- Secrets never enter logs; provider credentials live in a managed vault.
- Data retention policies per project; deletion is archival plus legal hold checks.
- Threat model reviewed per phase; pen tests before commercial launch.

### 15.9 Scalability and Reliability

- Stateless API tier, horizontally scaled behind the gateway.
- Workers autoscale per queue class and provider quota.
- Regional read replicas for graph and asset metadata.
- Graceful degradation: read-only mode, cached outputs, and queued writes.
- Target availability 99.9% for interactive surfaces, 99.5% for production queues.

### 15.10 Observability

- Distributed tracing from intent to artifact with run IDs.
- SLOs per capability: success rate, p95 latency, cost per artifact.
- Quality SLOs tracked alongside reliability SLOs.
- Anomaly alerts on identity drift, cost spikes, and provider error bursts.

### 15.11 Environments and Releases

- Local, preview, staging, production with identical schemas.
- Capability flags and canary rollouts by tenant tier.
- Forward-only migrations with expand-contract discipline.
- Release notes generated from the change log in this document.

### 15.12 Agent-Readable Service Contracts

Each service publishes a machine-readable contract: inputs, outputs, error classes, idempotency semantics, and SLO. Contracts are versioned and diffed like artifacts so agents can plan against them without reading implementation code.

---

## 16. Credits, Billing, and Metering

### 16.1 Economy Thesis

CreativeOS bills in credits because cost is variable and creative work is iterative. A credits model keeps price legible, protects margin against provider price changes, and gives producers a hard ceiling they can actually manage. The design borrows the clarity of modern product-credit systems: visible balance, per-action cost, predictable refill, and no surprise overage.

### 16.2 Plan Tiers

| Tier | Monthly credits | Seats | Concurrency | Rollover |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | 150 | 1 | 1 | none |
| Creator | 2,000 | 1 | 3 | 1 month |
| Studio | 12,000 | 5 | 8 | 2 months |
| Production | 60,000 | 20 | 24 | 3 months |
| Enterprise | pooled | unlimited | dedicated | negotiated |

### 16.3 Metering Model

- Cost is metered per capability run in credits, derived from provider cost plus platform margin.
- The estimate appears before execution; the charge is the actual, reconciled within a stated tolerance.
- Failed runs are refunded automatically unless provider cost was already incurred, which is disclosed.
- Batch and cached results are discounted and labeled.
- Deliverables and exports carry their own line items so distribution cost is never hidden inside generation.

### 16.5 Ledger Invariants

- Credits are double-entry: every debit has a credit and an attributed run.
- Balances are derived from the ledger, never stored as a mutable number.
- Every capability run writes a cost record before the artifact commits.
- Reconciliation runs hourly against provider invoices.

### 16.6 Budgets and Ceilings

- Project ceiling enforced at the gateway; no run may exceed it.
- Department budgets with soft warnings and hard stops.
- Forecast based on remaining scenes, shots, and iterations.
- Owner override requires explicit approval and is audited.

### 16.7 Refunds, Failures, and Disputes

- Automatic refund on platform failure before generation begins.
- Partial refund where a provider charged but produced an unusable artifact.
- Dispute window with artifact evidence attached.
- Every adjustment appears in the ledger with a reason code.

### 16.8 Abuse Prevention

- Rate limits per tenant and per capability class.
- Anomaly detection on burn rate and parallelism.
- Free-tier watermarking and deliverable restrictions.
- Repeated refund abuse escalates to manual review.

### 16.9 Transparency UX

- Balance, estimate, and burn rate visible in the presence bar.
- A pre-run cost sheet with cheaper alternatives.
- Per-project spend dashboard with forecast bands.
- No dark patterns: no auto-top-up, no expiry surprise, no hidden fees.

---

## 17. Technology Radar and Future Tools

### 17.1 Purpose

CreativeOS must absorb new technology without destabilizing production. The radar is the governed intake mechanism: emerging models, formats, and tools are evaluated, classified, and adopted on evidence rather than enthusiasm.

### 17.2 Radar Method

| Ring | Meaning | Commitment |
|---|---|---|
| Adopt | proven in production | supported, documented, default |
| Trial | promising with risk | behind flag, limited tenants |
| Assess | worth investigation | research budget, no promises |
| Hold | do not start new work | maintain only |

### 17.3 Horizons

- **Now (0-12 months):** continuity-locked generation, structured shot specs, credit metering, delivery validation.
- **Next (1-3 years):** real-time virtual production, agent-directed assembly, volumetric capture, interactive releases.
- **Later (3-7 years):** world simulation, autonomous production crews, neural asset compression, generated performance at scale.

### 17.4 Technology Entries

| Technology | Ring | Adoption rule |
|---|---|---|
| Diffusion video models | Adopt | supported with documented limits |
| Image diffusion models | Adopt | supported with documented limits |
| Speech synthesis | Adopt | supported with documented limits |
| Voice conversion | Trial | flagged rollout with exit criteria |
| Music generation | Trial | flagged rollout with exit criteria |
| Foley synthesis | Trial | flagged rollout with exit criteria |
| Neural upscaling | Adopt | supported with documented limits |
| Frame interpolation | Trial | flagged rollout with exit criteria |
| Motion transfer | Trial | flagged rollout with exit criteria |
| Gaussian splatting | Trial | flagged rollout with exit criteria |
| NeRF reconstruction | Assess | research spike, no production dependency |
| Light-field capture | Assess | research spike, no production dependency |
| Neural rendering | Assess | research spike, no production dependency |
| Digital humans | Trial | flagged rollout with exit criteria |
| Performance capture | Adopt | supported with documented limits |
| Facial rigging from video | Trial | flagged rollout with exit criteria |

### 17.5 Tool Catalogue

| Tool | Function | Owning studio |
|---|---|---|
| Shot Spec Compiler | turns intent into a structured, renderable shot record | Narrative Intelligence Studio |
| Continuity Diff | compares two takes across identity, wardrobe, light, and geography | Dialogue Studio |
| Look Translator | converts references into a governed look bible | Script Breakdown Studio |
| Prompt Distiller | reduces a shot spec to the minimal effective prompt per provider | World Architect Studio |
| Take Ranker | orders variants by rubric score and director preference | Universe Timeline Studio |
| Scene Assembler | builds a rough cut from approved takes and script beats | Lore Studio |
| Cue Sheet Builder | maps musical cues to picture and exports rights metadata | Franchise & IP Studio |
| Delivery Validator | checks masters against platform specifications | World Simulation Studio |
| Canon Linter | flags claims that contradict the universe bible | Character Architect Studio |
| Rights Resolver | traces every element to a license or consent | Character Psychology Studio |
| Cost Forecaster | predicts spend for the remaining production | Character Appearance Studio |
| Dependency Graph Viewer | shows what breaks if an artifact changes | Character Performance Studio |
| Reference Matcher | finds the closest approved visual reference | Character Relationship Studio |
| Identity Locker | pins a face and body across a sequence | Casting Studio |
| Wardrobe Tracker | enforces costume continuity per scene | Character Continuity Studio |
| Lighting Plot Builder | generates diagrams from scene intent | Director's Studio |
| Lens Comparator | previews focal length and distortion differences | Visual Direction Studio |
| Movement Previs Tool | simulates camera moves against blocking | Cinematography Studio |
| Foley Matcher | selects and aligns foley to action | Composition & Movement Studio |
| Ambience Weaver | builds continuous beds across cuts | Shot Design Studio |
| Score Syncer | aligns motif and hit points to the edit | Lighting Studio |
| Subtitle Aligner | times and styles captions per platform | Production Design Studio |
| Poster Composer | lays out key art with typography rules | Props, Costume & Makeup Studio |
| Trailer Beat Finder | selects highlights against a trailer structure | Storyboard & Previs Studio |
| Asset Reuse Advisor | suggests canon-safe reuse across titles | Image & Video Generation Studio |
| Export Packager | bundles masters, subtitles, and manifests | Generation Control Studio |
| Provenance Signer | signs manifests for delivery | VFX Studio |
| Review Thread Linker | ties notes to frames and artifacts | Animation Studio |
| Learning Injector | attaches the right lesson to the live decision | Sound Design Studio |
| Budget Scenario Modeler | compares cost outcomes across plans | Voice & Dubbing Studio |

### 17.6 Evaluation Gates

- Quality: must clear the benchmark reel at the target tier.
- Cost: must fit the credit class it is priced into.
- Reliability: p95 latency and failure rate within SLO.
- Rights: provider terms compatible with commercial delivery.
- Operability: fallback path exists before adoption.

### 17.7 Emerging Formats

- Interactive film with branching narratives and state persistence.
- Volumetric and immersive releases for headset and venue.
- Episodic micro-formats for vertical platforms.
- Game cinematics with engine-native delivery.
- Localized variant production at territory scale.

## 18. Non-Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target |
|---|---|---|
| NFR-01 | Interactive latency | p50 < 2s, p95 < 6s |
| NFR-02 | Long job resumability | 100% after disconnection |
| NFR-03 | Asset discoverability | one search query from anywhere |
| NFR-04 | Reproducibility | identical inputs, seed, provider version reproduce lineage |
| NFR-05 | Cost control | per-project hard ceiling enforced |
| NFR-06 | Audit completeness | every mutation emits an audit event |
| NFR-07 | Permissions | RBAC at studio and asset level |
| NFR-08 | Export validation | delivery profile check before release |
| NFR-09 | Provider independence | any capability runs on at least two providers where available |
| NFR-10 | Data residency | project-level region pinning |
| NFR-11 | Interface frame rate | 60fps target, 30fps floor on low-power devices |
| NFR-12 | First meaningful content | under 1s warm, stage-labelled skeleton beyond 400ms |
| NFR-13 | Input parity | every action operable by keyboard, touch, and voice where text-driven |
| NFR-14 | Accessibility | WCAG 2.2 AA across all themes and modes |
| NFR-15 | Companion restraint | at most one unprompted suggestion per decision point |
| NFR-16 | Reversibility | 100% of AI actions undoable, forkable, or comparable |

### Appendix D.3 Risk Register

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Scope expansion outpaces quality | high | phase gates and usage-based prioritization |
| Provider pricing changes erode margin | high | credit classes and multi-provider routing |
| Continuity drift at long sequence length | high | identity locking and per-shot rubric |
| Rights ambiguity blocks commercial release | high | consent ledger and delivery blocking |
| Companion oversteps authorship | medium | trust ladder and refusal policy |
| Cost overrun on heavy VFX | medium | shot-level ceilings and ROI re-renders |
| Data residency requirements multiply | medium | regional pinning and per-tenant keys |
| Model quality regressions after updates | medium | pinned versions and benchmark gate |
| Collaboration conflicts on artifacts | medium | version graph and approval routing |
| Onboarding complexity | medium | progressive disclosure and first-five-minutes design |
| Benchmark ceiling hard to prove | medium | public scorecard and blind panel |
| Talent expectations mismatch | low | artist-grade controls and craft academy |

### Appendix D.4 Metric Dictionary

| Metric | Definition | Target |
|---|---|---|
| `time_to_first_artifact` | minutes from signup to first approved artifact | under 5 |
| `project_completion_rate` | projects reaching a locked master | over 40% |
| `continuity_defects_per_100_shots` | detected drift failures | under 3 |
| `shot_pass_rate_by_tier` | shots clearing their quality tier first pass | over 65% for Q2 |
| `companion_accept_rate` | suggestions accepted | over 35% |
| `cost_per_finished_minute` | credits per delivered minute | trending down |
| `approval_turnaround` | median hours to decision | under 24h |
| `asset_reuse_rate` | assets reused across titles | over 60% in franchises |
| `render_retry_rate` | jobs requiring retry | under 10% |
| `p95_capability_latency` | end-to-end run latency | within tier budget |
| `support_tickets_per_100_projects` | defect signal from users | trending down |
| `refund_rate` | credits refunded | under 5% |

### Appendix D.5 Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| D-001 | Studios as modules with one graph | prevents fragmentation and duplicated truth |
| D-002 | Generation provider abstraction | protects margin and avoids lock-in |
| D-003 | Companion cannot self-approve | preserves authorship and audit integrity |
| D-004 | Credits instead of subscription-only | aligns price with variable cost |
| D-005 | Quality tiers rather than a single bar | makes tradeoffs explicit per use case |
| D-006 | Canon as a governed graph | enables franchises without contradiction |
| D-007 | Progressive disclosure over dashboards | protects first-run success |
| D-008 | Design system owned separately | keeps this document behavioral, not visual |
